jobs.title: Principal Design Engineer - Mechanical Equipment (80-100%)
jobs.description:
• Engineering Solutions: You provide technical leadership and expertise in the industrialization of mechanical components and systems, transforming concepts into integrated, robust and reliable industrial equipment products. You deliver innovative engineering solutions that ensure proper validation and enable scalable, high-quality manufacturing and serial production.

• Product Design & CAD: You technically lead, create, and optimize product designs, using CAD tools (e.g., SolidWorks) to develop integrated systems, component assemblies and 2D manufacturing drawings. You ensure full technical readiness of the products according to the development plan.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration and Leadership: You work closely with cross-functional teams and act as the expert for mechanical design, component integration, and manufacturability. You mentor less experienced engineers, provide technical guidance in decision-making, and manage external design resources to ensure their efficient integration into the development process.

• Quality Assurance & Technical Readiness: You ensure the technical correctness and completeness of the design, from specifications to manufacturing drawings and bills of materials, with a strong focus on compliance with organizational and industrial standards.

• Approval of Technical Documentation: You take full ownership as the approval authority for technical product documentation. This includes the review and approval of engineering drawings and the corresponding bill of materials. You lead design review presentations and uphold high standards to ensure accurate, traceable, and audit-ready development documentation that supports compliance and continuous product improvement.

• Prototype Development & Testing: You define validation units, coordinate their fabrication, and participate in testing activities. You ensure that all test findings are transferred into product improvements.

Requirements:
• Education & Engineering Expertise: You hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering and bring deep, expert level expertise in engineering fundamentals and complex system development.

• Advanced Mechanical Engineering Application: You have a proven ability to apply advanced engineering principles,
 development methodologies, and analytical techniques to the design of large industrial equipment components.

• Mechanical Design & Manufacturing Knowledge: With 12+ years designing mechanical components for industrial machinery, you bring expert metal and sheet metal design skills, strong knowledge of key manufacturing processes, and proficiency in DFMA, material selection, and regulatory compliance (with internal and industrial standards). You deliver robust, reliable design solutions.

• CAD Proficiency & Technical Skills: You are proficient in designing mechanical components using CAD and in creating high quality technical drawings. You are experienced in applying geometric dimensioning and tolerancing chains and understand the corresponding manufacturing processes.

• Attention to Detail & Problem-Solving: You have strong attention to detail, excellent organizational skills, and a passion for problem-solving and creative engineering.

• Communication & Teamwork: You communicate effectively in English, collaborate confidently with cross-functional teams, and enjoy mentoring and guiding less experienced engineers. You contribute to a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement, while actively expanding your own expertise and advancing your engineering career.

Our promise: At Climeworks, you are accepted for who you are, and we are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply – regardless of background, identity, or experience. Studies show that women and individuals from minority backgrounds often only apply for jobs when they meet 100% of the listed criteria. If this sounds like you, don’t hold back. If you think you’d make a great fit for this role, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t check every single box. Let’s tackle one of humankind’s greatest challenges together.

What we offer:

• Time Off: Enjoy 25 paid vacation days every year, plus public holidays.

• Flexibility: Work how it suits you best. We offer a hybrid work setup and up to 4 weeks of remote work annually within any EU country.

• Ownership: Fair base pay paired with an equity package – because your contributions matter.

• Family Support: Inclusive parental leave.

• Continuous Learning: Dedicated budget to invest in your professional growth.

jobs.title: Lead Mechanical Engineer (100%)
jobs.description:
• Specifications and design : You lead the development of fit-for-purpose mechanical specifications, design philosophies, and basis of design for execution Globally. You ensure owner requirements are clearly defined, documented, and communicated to contractors, and validate design assumptions against operability, safety, and applicable regulatory expectations. This includes defining a pressure equipment compliance pathway (e.g., registration and lifecycle documentation expectations) suitable for local and regional execution.

• Cold-weather and constructability: As our next DAC plant is planned for Alberta, Canada, you incorporate Alberta (or similar) climate conditions into mechanical design and execution planning (freeze protection, winterization, insulation/heat tracing philosophy, drainage/low-point management, cold start/commissioning constraints). You ensure the design is constructable and able to operate and be maintained through winter conditions, including consideration of temporary works, winter work sequencing, and interface constraints with cold-weather civil activities.

• Contractor management : You review and approve contractor submissions, enforce owner requirements, provide technical clarifications, and ensure adherence to schedule, quality, safety, and operability. You set clear expectations for execution methods, field quality controls, and turnover documentation needed for safe operation and maintenance.

• Innovation and cost optimization : You develop innovative engineering solutions to identify cost-saving opportunities without compromising quality or safety. You focus on design-to-construct decisions appropriate for local boundary conditions (e.g., modularization readiness, reduced field welds, optimized layout, local climactic conditions, access and maintenance).

• Interface management : You assure strong integration with process, civil, electrical, and O&M disciplines to achieve seamless and optimized designs. You proactively manage cross-discipline interfaces.

• Regulatory and stakeholder awareness: Where relevant, you support alignment of mechanical scope assumptions with local permitting and application needs for energy/industrial facilities and infrastructure interfaces.

• Documentation and knowledge management : You maintain thorough records of technical decisions, design bases, vendor information, and lessons learned for future operational use, including pressure equipment records and lifecycle documentation expectations.

Requirements:
• Educational background: You hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering.

• Professional experience: You bring at least 10 years of experience in process plants in cold weather climates, as a mechanical static equipment engineer, with proven expertise in API and ASME equipment such as heat exchangers, columns, pressure vessels, storage tanks, and packaged auxiliary equipment.

• Mandatory requirement: Demonstrated, hands‑on experience with cold‑weather industrial plant design and execution, including winterization, freeze protection, and constructability planning for winter conditions (e.g., Canada, Nordics, Northern US).

• Project experience: You have hands-on involvement in at least one full-cycle project in the chemical, petrochemical, or renewables industry, covering all phases from FEED and detailed design to construction, commissioning and start-up-preferably in cold-weather or remote/seasonally constrained execution environments.

• Work style: You are precise, adaptable, and reliable, with a proactive and solution-oriented approach. You are comfortable driving decisions and owning them in the office and under field constraints, including winter productivity and schedule risk.

• Communication: You are confident in presenting to executive audiences and EPC contractors, translating technical content into clear, actionable information.

• Languages & travel : You are fluent in English and ready to travel up to 60% of your time depending on which phase the project is (including extended site presence in Alberta, Canada).

• Documentation and knowledge management : You maintain thorough records of technical decisions, design bases, vendor information, and lessons learned for future operational use, including pressure equipment records and lifecycle documentation expectations.

• Patent Advisory and Innovation Mining: Your mission at Climeworks is to advise on patenting and related matters as well as to foster sustainable innovation mining across the organization.

• IP and Inventor Enablement: You enable the management of IP topics by guiding inventors and ensuring readiness for future projects.

• Technology and Product Landscape Monitoring: You continuously monitor Climeworks’ product innovations and the evolving technology landscape.

• Inventor and Expert Interface: You serve as the essential bridge between inventors and innovation protection experts, ensuring efficient communication and collaboration.

• Patent Portfolio and Scientific Analysis: You dive deep into Climeworks’ patent portfolio and relevant scientific literature to provide strong technical insights.

• Core Technology Ownership: You own core technology domains with a focus on patent filing and ongoing maintenance.

• Continuous Improvement: You refine and streamline Climeworks’ innovation mining and protection approaches, ensuring the company remains an industry leader.

Requirements:
• Scientific and Technical Foundation: You possess a scientific or engineering background and bring a broad, practical understanding of diverse technical topics with an open and curious technical mindset.

• Experience: You bring 5+ years of experience in patent prosecution and the active management of patent portfolios.

• Working Style: You are trustworthy, reliable, and excel at driving projects to completion independently, supported by a strong strategic mindset.

• Adaptability and Agility: You adapt swiftly to new challenges and can shift focus as priorities evolve in a dynamic environment.

• Language Proficiency: You are proficient in English, both spoken and written.

Nice to have:

• You are a qualified patent attorney (CH, EU and/or US) with solid knowledge of EU and US patent laws.

• You have patent litigation experience.

• You might have had in-house roles in multinational companies.

• You have robust expertise in engineering, chemistry, or both.

• You have experience driving cross-functional projects to successful conclusion.

• You can converse in German.

jobs.title: Intern in Sorbent Characterization (100%)
jobs.description:
• Your role: As an intern, you will support the evaluation and development of sorbents and sorbent structures for DAC. You will gain hands-on experience in lab-based testing, data analysis, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

• Lab Assessments: You collaborate within an integrated team to carry out lab-based assessments, including adsorption characterization, accelerated lifetime testing, and process-relevant evaluations of novel materials.

• Material Stability: You investigate material stability by testing under accelerated aging conditions to simulate long-term performance.

• Sorbent Characterization: You characterize sorbent behaviour by measuring unary and binary isotherms under controlled conditions.

• Independent Work: You work independently on targeted work packages to understand how material properties influence DAC performance.

• Method Development: You contribute to the development, refinement, and validation of experimental methods to ensure reliable and reproducible testing outcomes.

• Documentation & Communication: You validate, troubleshoot, and clearly document your work to ensure effective communication across interdisciplinary development teams at Climeworks.

Requirements:
• Education & Experience: You have a bachelor’s degree and/or are working towards a master’s degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or similar.

• Technical Skills: You enjoy working hands-on in the lab, and you have some classroom or other experience with any of the following: characterization of porous materials (N₂ adsorption, Hg porosimetry, DVS, etc.), adsorption characterization (breakthrough testing).

• Additional Knowledge: Familiarity with CO₂ capture is beneficial but not required.

• Mindset: You are eager to learn new concepts, skills, and tools that you might need to complete your assignments.

• Working Style: You are reliable, motivated, solution-oriented, concise, and have a structured working style.

• Availability: You are available for a 6-month internship with a start date preferably in August 2026 or shortly thereafter.

jobs.description:
• Specifications and design : You develop and lead our Piping Engineering & Plant Layout Team, making sure it delivers on all project requirements in a fit-for-purpose manner Globally. You ensure owner requirements are clearly defined, documented, and communicated to contractors, and validate design assumptions against operability, safety, and applicable regulatory expectations. This includes defining piping and plant layouts suitable for local and regional execution.

• Contractor management : You review and approve contractor submissions, enforce owner requirements, provide technical clarifications, and ensure adherence to schedule, quality, safety, and operability. You set clear expectations for execution methods, field quality controls, and turnover documentation needed for safe operation and maintenance.

• Innovation and cost optimization : You develop innovative engineering solutions to identify cost-saving opportunities without compromising quality or safety. You focus on design-to-construct decisions appropriate for local boundary conditions (e.g., modularization readiness, reduced field welds, optimized layout, local climactic conditions, access and maintenance.

• Interface management : You assure strong integration with process, civil, electrical, mechanical and O&M disciplines to achieve seamless and optimized designs. You proactively manage cross-discipline interfaces.

• Regulatory and stakeholder awareness: You support alignment of piping and plant layout scope assumptions with local permitting and application needs for energy/industrial facilities and infrastructure interfaces.

• Documentation and knowledge management : You maintain thorough records of technical decisions, design bases, vendor information, and lessons learned for future operational use.

• Cold-weather and constructability : As our next DAC plant is planned for Alberta, Canada, you incorporate Alberta (or similar) climate conditions into piping and plant layout design and execution planning (freeze protection, winterization, insulation/heat tracing philosophy, drainage/low-point management, cold start/commissioning constraints). You ensure the design is constructable and able to operate and be maintained through winter conditions, including consideration of temporary works, winter work sequencing, and interface constraints with cold-weather civil activities.

Requirements:
• Educational background: You hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering or any related discipline.

• Professional experience: You bring at least 10 years of experience in process plants in cold weather climates, as a piping and plant layout engineer, with understanding of current standards and directives in mechanical, piping and civil engineering.

• Project experience: You have hands-on involvement in at least one full-cycle project in the chemical, petrochemical, or renewables industry, covering all phases from FEED and detailed design to construction, commissioning and start-up-preferably in cold-weather or remote/seasonally constrained execution environments.

• Work style: You are precise, adaptable, and reliable, with a proactive and solution-oriented approach. You are comfortable driving decisions and owning them in the office and under field constraints, including winter productivity and schedule risk.

• Communication: You are confident in presenting to executive audiences and EPC contractors, translating technical content into clear, actionable information.

• Languages & travel : You are fluent in English and ready to travel up to 60% of your time (including extended site presence in Alberta, Canada during peak design, engineering, construction and commissioning periods).

jobs.description:
In this role, you will apply deep synthetic chemistry expertise to design, synthesize and evaluate next-generation sorbent materials for Direct Air Capture. You will take scientific ownership of early-stage material innovation, connect synthesis decisions with performance data and help identify the most promising sorbent concepts for further development. You will play a central role in coordinating across stakeholders to ensure alignment of research priorities, technical development and broader organization goals. The role is ideal for a hands-on chemist who enjoys driving technical work independently while collaborating closely with experts across characterization, engineering, scale-up, legal, and external innovation.

This role is a strong fit if you:

• You are a hands-on synthetic chemist, ideally with experience in material synthesis or functional material development.

• You enjoy working as an individual contributor and technical expert, while effectively coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders.

• You want to stay close to lab-based experimentation, synthesis, characterization, and scientific problem-solving.

• You are motivated by early-stage R&D and material innovation, with a passion for dynamic, discovery-driven environments.

What you will do:

• Design and synthesize new sorbent materials: You develop and improve sorbent chemistries for Direct Air Capture, with a focus on performance, durability, cost and scalability.

• Evaluate material performance: You plan experiments, analyze characterization and adsorption data, and connect synthesis decisions with structure-property relationships.

• Identify promising concepts: You screen internal and external sorbent concepts against clear technical, commercial, regulatory, scalability, and IP-related criteria.

• Drive hands-on laboratory work: You run safe, well-documented synthesis and testing campaigns, maintain structured material data, and translate results into recommendations.

• Collaborate and coordinate across disciplines: You work closely with experts in characterization, engineering, scale-up, legal, patents and external innovation to move the most promising sorbent concepts forward.

Requirements:
• Synthetic chemistry expertise: You have strong hands-on experience in synthetic organic or inorganic chemistry. You have experience in porous, functionalized, polymeric or amine-based. Experience with other sorbent-relevant materials is a plus.

• Relevant experience: You bring at least 5 years of experience in synthetic chemistry, material synthesis or material development, including applied R&D, start-up, industrial or technology development experience.

• Chemistry background: You hold an advanced degree in organic, inorganic, synthetic, materials chemistry or a related field. A PhD is a plus.

• Scientific ownership: You are comfortable leading your own workstreams, interpreting data critically and translating findings into clear recommendations.

• Clear communication: You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders and are proficient in English.

jobs.description:
You will lead Climeworks’ global Health, Safety, Security and Environmental (HSSE) function, ensuring a consistent and high-performing safety culture across our production facilities, testing sites and corporate environments. At the same time, you will oversee corporate facilities and workplace operations, ensuring our headquarters operate safely, efficiently and to the highest standards.
 This is a critical leadership role at the heart of our scaling journey, combining enterprise risk ownership with hands-on operational execution.

• HSSE Strategy & Policies: You define and implement Climeworks’ global HSSE (health, safety, security & environment) strategy, standards and policies across all locations, ensuring a consistent and forward-looking approach to HSSE standards.

• Safety Program Ownership: You own and continuously improve the safety program across production facilities, testing sites, construction sites, and corporate workplaces, embedding a strong safety culture throughout the organization.

• Regulatory Engagement: You liaise with regulatory bodies across all jurisdictions where Climeworks operates, ensuring full compliance and maintaining strong, collaborative relationships with authorities.

• Executive Reporting: You act as the accountable owner of safety performance (e.g. LTIR/TRIR), including executive reporting and driving improvement actions.

• Corporate Facility Management Leadership: You provide strategic hands-on leadership in Facility Management at the Climeworks HQ in Opfikon, while sharing good practices with other Climeworks locations. Note: Direct site management of production and testing facilities is outside your remit.

• Stakeholder Management: You act as the primary point of contact for all internal and external facility- and site-related matters, collaborating closely with subsidiaries and external stakeholders.

• Financial & Contract Management: You oversee the financial and commercial management of HSE and facilities-related contracts, ensuring cost efficiency and strong contractual performance.

• Safety and corporate workplace integration: You ensure full alignment between HSSE standard and corporate workplace execution.

• Leadership & Organizational Development: You lead and coach HSSE and Facilities Management teams, fostering a strong culture of quality, accountability, safety, and customer service across the organization. Act as the single point of accountability for safety and workplace operations across the company.

Requirements:
• Education & Qualifications: You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health and Safety or in a related field, providing a solid academic foundation for this role.

• Professional Experience: You bring over 10 years of industry experience in HSSE leadership within industrial, energy or process environments.

jobs.title: Monitoring & Alerting Engineering Intern (100%)
jobs.description:
• End-to-End Ownership: You take ownership of a real, end-to-end project, from understanding operational needs to delivering a standardized, scalable alerting framework.

• Stakeholder Needs: You engage with different teams to identify critical monitoring requirements and analyzing which events truly require alerting versus noise reduction.

• Grafana Alerting: You build and configure alerts in Grafana based on data from PostgreSQL, defining thresholds, triggers, and escalation logic.

• Cross-Team Alignment: You collaborate across facilities and backbone teams to drive consistency and harmonization of monitoring approaches.

• Alert Communication: You create and organize Microsoft Teams alert channels aligned with the right audience and ensure alerts reach the appropriate stakeholders at the right time.

• Standardization: You develop consistent naming conventions and alert phrasing, ensuring clarity, usability, and actionable messaging.

• Data & Queries: You write and optimize SQL queries for alerting logic and work with data pipelines feeding Grafana dashboards.

Requirements:
• Educational Background: You are pursuing or have recently completed (within the last year) a BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Data Engineering, IT, or a related field.

• Technical Foundation: You have basic knowledge of SQL and data analysis and are highly interested in observability, monitoring, or infrastructure systems.

• Collaboration & Communication: You have good communication skills and are comfortable working with multiple stakeholders.

• Adaptability & Creativity: You demonstrate flexibility, adaptability, and creativity, especially when working with unknown or incomplete information.

• Working Style & Ownership: You are reliable, performance-driven, maintain a structured way of working, and are proactive in driving topics independently.

• Teamwork & Independence: You thrive in fast-paced team environments and are equally effective when working independently.

• Language Skills: You are fluent in English; German is an advantage.

• Availability: You are available for a full-time 6-month internship, ideally starting in September 2026.

jobs.description:
• Growth Engine Support: You support the Growth team in building and operating the engine behind the go-to-market strategy, contributing to demand generation, deal progression, and the preparation of high-quality materials for senior customer engagements.

• Sales Enablement: You support the delivery of growth initiatives by preparing sales materials and helping opportunities move smoothly through the funnel.

• Sales Operations: You help maintain CRM and ERP systems, keeping customer and opportunity data up to date while supporting the team with accurate pipeline and order information.

• Events & Engagements: You assist in the planning and execution of customer events, climate conferences, and senior stakeholder engagements.

• Customer Success: You support the preparation of materials, documentation, and customer-facing updates for contracted carbon removal deliveries.

• Commercial Readiness: You contribute to RFP responses, presentations, customer portal activations, and communication campaigns by preparing inputs, coordinating details, and ensuring materials are ready on time.

• Market Intelligence: You research carbon market trends, corporate procurement patterns, competitor activity, and customer insights to help inform commercial priorities.

• Cross-functional Coordination: You support the handling of inbound sales requests and coordinate with Legal, Finance, and other teams on contracts, NDAs, invoices, and customer-related follow-ups.

Requirements:
• Education & Career Aspirations: You are currently pursuing or have recently (within the past year) completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in sustainability, business, or a related field, and are eager to develop your skills in sales and commercial areas.

• Commercial Awareness: You possess a solid understanding of commercial dynamics, including contracts, business cases, event management, and corporate decision-making processes.

• Climate Action & Sustainability: You have a strong interest in climate action and sustainability, ideally complemented by prior exposure to carbon markets or related initiatives.

• Technical Proficiency: You are tech-savvy, with proficiency in Microsoft Office and CRM tools, and you demonstrate strong presentation skills.

• Analytical Skills: You are analytical and detail-oriented, with the ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights.

• Work Ethic & Mindset: You are self-motivated, solution-oriented, and thrive in a fast-paced, multicultural environment.
